 Petrol, Diesel Prices Unlikely to Fall Immediately, Says Suresh Gopi 
 18 Nov 2026 
 2 Min Read 
 CW Team 
 Share 
 -->
 Union Minister of State for Petroleum and Natural Gas Suresh Gopi said an immediate reduction in petrol and diesel prices was not feasible, citing Rs. 420 bn in losses incurred by oil companies amid the West Asia conflict and disruptions in petroleum supplies. The minister was speaking to reporters at Chennai’s Meenambakkam airport on Monday.
 Gopi said oil companies would first need to account for their accumulated losses before reducing retail fuel prices. He did not specify the period covered by the loss figure. He also said state governments could reduce taxes on petrol and diesel, noting that fuel prices vary because of differences in value-added tax and sales tax rates.
 The minister acknowledged disruptions in petroleum supplies and said the government was taking steps to resolve them. The remarks followed several interventions aimed at managing fuel prices and availability during the West Asia conflict. On March 27, the Centre reduced excise duty on petrol and diesel by Rs. 10 per litre each after international crude prices rose sharply.
 The Petroleum Ministry said the duty reduction was intended to offset part of the losses incurred by public sector oil marketing companies, including Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum Corporation and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation, rather than directly lower retail prices. In a written reply to the Lok Sabha on July 30, Gopi said petrol and diesel prices were market-determined and that public sector oil companies were responsible for pricing decisions.
 He said India’s crude oil basket rose from $69 per barrel in February to $136.68 in March and stood at $103.33 on July 23. The government also temporarily limited diesel purchases at retail outlets from June 12 to 200 litres per customer or vehicle per day to address diversion, hoarding and black marketing. The restriction was withdrawn on July 1 after a review of supplies. Separately, Karnataka Industries Minister MB Patil raised concerns about ethanol procurement and called for an investigation into alleged irregularities in the blending process.
